checkpoint.title: YAML Semantic Change Review Implementation Handoff

repository.branch_strategy: Create the implementation branch from the exact base commit after confirming origin/main still contains it. If main or tracked product bytes have moved, reconcile and refresh this request before editing.
repository.reconciliation_rule: Repository reality wins. Preserve unknown edits and fail closed on material schema, YAML workflow, or ownership-boundary contradictions.

accepted_specification.title: YAML Semantic Change Review Specification
accepted_specification.behavior: Preview must provide a deterministic, ID-aware semantic summary of how the complete validated DesignDocument differs from the immutable document captured when the YAML dialog opened.
accepted_specification.authority_boundary: The summary is a local review aid. Existing strict parsing, explicit Preview then Apply, server validation, and optimistic revision checks remain authoritative.

authority.required_next_authorization: Explicitly authorize the bounded product implementation against this request after reconciling the then-current base.

included_scope: Add one DesignDocument-specific shared semantic comparison utility.
Integrate the summary into the existing YAML Preview workflow without changing Validate or Apply authority.
Present aggregate and bounded detailed changes accessibly in the existing YAML modal on desktop and mobile.
Add focused shared unit tests and YAML browser workflow tests.
Update only the smallest directly owning behavioral documentation.
Update E2E test-plan routing only if the new shared owner would otherwise select the wrong lane.
excluded_scope: Canonical persistence or stored document changes
REST, API, MCP, WebMCP, CLI, import, or export contract changes
Revision, authorization, ownership, publication, or collaboration changes
Raw YAML/text diff as the primary semantic model
Selective hunk apply, generalized history/version-control UI, undo redesign, or automatic merge
Presence, WebSockets, collaborative YAML editing, or conflict-resolution redesign
Dependency-security remediation or unrelated dependency upgrades
Unrelated accessibility work, editor redesign, refactoring, deployment, or release

semantic_model.baseline: A structured clone or otherwise immutable reference-equivalent DesignDocument captured when YamlSourceDialog opens.
semantic_model.candidate: The DesignDocument returned by the existing parseDocumentYaml path after strict YAML and documentSchema validation.
ignored_noise: YAML comments, formatting, scalar spelling, and mapping-key order
metadata.updatedAt when it is the only semantic difference
id_aware_collections: nodes within each page by id
nested collections that expose a repository-schema stable id, name, or other explicitly unique identifier
semantic_model.non_id_collections: Where the current schema permits no stable identity, do not invent one. Compare deterministically by structural value and index, report the owning field/collection as modified, and classify reorder separately only when exact element equality establishes a safe permutation.
semantic_model.paths: Use user-comprehensible collection names and stable IDs where present, for example pages[home].nodes[hero].text. Never use array position as entity identity when a stable ID exists.
semantic_model.ordering: Sort summary groups in a fixed documented product order and detail rows by classification, semantic path, then stable identifier so identical inputs always produce byte-equivalent summary objects.

limits.raw_values_default: Do not render raw before/after values by default.
limits.privacy: Never dump data URLs, asset URLs, embedded/binary-like strings, large arrays/objects, or complete user content into the summary.

requirements.statement: Implement a shared, synchronous, deterministic, side-effect-free comparison function accepting two schema-valid DesignDocument values and returning typed aggregate counts plus bounded detail rows.
Match collections by repository-defined stable identity wherever available; classify stable-identity reorder independently from add/remove and never infer absent identity semantics.

Report complete-document changes across document fields, theme, characters, pages, nodes, assets, design system, presentation, timeline, and schemaVersion 2 boards/paintings while suppressing serialization-only noise.
Run comparison only after existing strict YAML/schema validation during Preview; source edits invalidate both visual preview and semantic summary.
Keep Preview local and non-mutating. Apply must continue sending the complete parsed document through the existing revision and optional brief-revision guarded save path.
On stale-revision or save failure, preserve the edited YAML and last valid semantic summary for reconciliation and retain the existing actionable error behavior.

Present aggregate-first user-facing groups, unchanged state, bounded details, and explicit truncation without relying on color; preserve keyboard order, focus visibility, status/error semantics, long-path wrapping, and existing mobile full-screen behavior.
Reuse current DesignDocument/YAML contracts and add no runtime dependency, migration, public contract, persistence, authorization, or provider behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: For a valid candidate, Preview clearly reports complete aggregate added, removed, modified, and reordered counts plus bounded semantic paths for meaningful changes across the complete document, including changes outside page 1.
Pages, nodes, assets, characters, boards, paintings, timeline tracks, and other schema collections with stable identity are matched by that identity rather than array index.
Pure reorder of stable-ID entities is reported as reorder and is not misreported as removal plus addition; modification combined with reorder remains visible as both applicable effects.

Collections without stable IDs use deterministic structural/index fallback without invented identity; additions, removals, nested modifications, and safely detectable exact-value permutations are classified consistently.
Semantically equivalent documents report unchanged despite YAML formatting/comments/key order or object insertion order; metadata.updatedAt alone creates no user-visible change.

Invalid or unsupported YAML cannot produce a semantic preview or reach Apply; editing source after Preview clears the rendered preview and summary; Preview performs no persistence or canonical editor mutation.
Correct-revision Apply continues to save the complete validated document through the existing path, while stale revision is rejected without losing edited source or the last valid summary.
Repeated comparison of identical before/after inputs yields deep-equal ordered output and neither input is mutated, including frozen-input tests.

The summary is usable by keyboard and assistive technology, does not rely on color, wraps long paths/content, exposes truncation, and remains operable at representative 375, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixel layouts.

Existing Validate/Preview/Apply, strict YAML, JSON persistence/workflows, schema v1/v2, revision conflicts, import/export, CLI, authorization, and production build regressions remain green with no dependency, lockfile, migration, or public-contract change.

new_expected.purpose: DesignDocument-specific typed semantic comparison and deterministic bounded output
Unit coverage for semantics, determinism, immutability, limits, and schema versions

existing_expected.purpose: Capture opening baseline, generate/clear summary with Preview, preserve summary on save conflict, and render accessible review UI
Aggregate/detail hierarchy, wrapping, truncation, and responsive presentation
Non-mutation, semantic presentation, invalidation, Apply, stale revision, accessibility, and mobile/desktop workflow
Add the new shared owner to the existing yaml-source area unless current routing already selects the intended lane
Small owning behavioral clarification if this remains the canonical YAML workflow documentation

conditional_documentation.condition: Only if repository documentation ownership shows the user guide directly promises YAML Preview behavior
Only when a public guide/source claim changes

target_files.unexpected_change_stop_rule: Stop for re-authorization before changing server routes, schema owners, persistence, CLI/MCP/WebMCP, package.json, package-lock.json, migrations, generated bundles, or unrelated product files.

dependency_expectations.security_debt: Eight existing high-severity npm audit findings remain deferred. Inspection shows they are in Cloudflare Puppeteer/extract-zip, Wrangler/Miniflare/Sharp, and PptxGenJS/image-size chains, not in the proposed pure DesignDocument comparison or React YAML-dialog path.
dependency_expectations.fail_closed_rule: If implementation introduces archive extraction, image parsing, renderer execution, untrusted executable content, or any affected audited dependency into the summary path, stop and open a security-specific blocker rather than continuing.

covers: existing JSON/YAML CLI and export behavior

verification_plan.procedure: Generate changed paths and run the PowerShell-safe equivalent of npm run test:e2e -- $(node scripts/test-plan.mjs --format=args). At minimum preserve yaml-source-ui plus always-run security coverage. Record only browsers actually executed.

Inspect representative unchanged, small, reordered, multi-page, and over-200-change summaries at 375/768/1024/1440 widths, keyboard-only operation, long paths, zoom/text scaling, and stale-save recovery.

rollback.strategy: Revert only the focused change-summary utility, YAML dialog integration/styles, corresponding tests/test-plan mapping, and directly owning documentation.
rollback.data: No migration or persisted-data rollback is required.
preserve: Merged strict YAML codec and existing authoring/import/export/CLI behavior
Canonical JSON DesignDocument persistence and revisions
Historical Steward evidence and unrelated user changes

known_risks.risk: Naive recursion misclassifies ID-aware reorder or emits noisy paths.
known_risks.mitigation: Explicit collection ownership, stable-ID maps, separate order comparison, deterministic tests, and no generic diff abstraction.

known_risks.risk: Large documents overwhelm memory or the modal.
known_risks.mitigation: Schema-valid bounded inputs, aggregate-first processing, 200 rendered rows, deterministic truncation, and large-document tests.

known_risks.risk: Before/after values expose private URLs, data URLs, or substantial user content.
known_risks.mitigation: Paths and classifications by default; no raw values unless short primitive disclosure is explicitly reviewed and bounded.

known_risks.risk: Users mistake the semantic summary or first-page render for authoritative save validation or complete visual coverage.
known_risks.mitigation: Label as a local review, retain explicit Apply, disclose complete semantic versus first-page visual coverage, and preserve server checks.

known_risks.risk: Existing audit debt becomes conflated with this feature.
known_risks.mitigation: No dependency changes; keep the eight findings deferred and fail closed if an affected dependency enters the implementation path.

unresolved_non_blocking.question: Should short primitive before/after values appear by default?
unresolved_non_blocking.resolution_rule: Start with paths, classifications, and aggregate counts only. Add bounded primitive values only if implementation UX review demonstrates clear benefit without privacy/noise regression.

unresolved_non_blocking.question: How much stable-ID reorder detail should be shown?
unresolved_non_blocking.resolution_rule: Show aggregate reorder count and a bounded owning collection/identifier list; do not render a complete move script.

unresolved_non_blocking.question: Should Apply be disabled when the candidate is semantically unchanged?
unresolved_non_blocking.resolution_rule: Preserve current enabled behavior unless focused implementation review proves disabling improves clarity without changing accepted workflow semantics.

unresolved_non_blocking.question: Should nested schema collections keyed by name/time be treated as stable identities?
unresolved_non_blocking.resolution_rule: Only use a field when the current schema/validator explicitly guarantees uniqueness in that owning collection; otherwise use the non-ID fallback.
